learning_outcomes.text: Solve spatial problems and conceive technical forms, characteristic of creative project and industrial design activities.
Conceive the operation and the assembly and disassembly operations of mechanical assemblies.
Apply Technical Drawing Standards and the symbology specific to elements, systems and technical schemes, of structures and industrial installations.
Express and communicate technical ideas and forms, own or others', through freehand sketches, technical drawings and models created with drawing instruments and CAD programs.
Elaborate graphic technical documentation with a professional sense, in the context of technical project and industrial design activities.

syllabus_topics: Installations on plans. Installation scheme. Electrical drawing in residential buildings. Power and control schemes for industrial installations with electric motors.

Surfaces. Concepts and general layouts. Polyhedra. Developable ruled surfaces. Warped ruled surfaces. Surfaces of revolution. Other significant surfaces of technical application. Intersections between surfaces.

Standardized representation of industrial parts. Technical drawings. Assemblies and exploded views. Surface qualities. Tolerances and fits. Mechanical joining elements and systems. Threaded joints. Welded and riveted joints. Other standardized joining systems and accessories. Basic mechanical elements or components. Mechanisms for displacement and rotation transformation.
teaching_methods: Individual work session in medium group
Group work session in medium group
Analysis, synthesis, and study of information and documentation

assessment_methods.method: In-class tests (Tests and reports of experimental work)
Written exams (Long-answer tests and tests and reports of experimental work)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 points is required. This score is calculated by weighting the Written Exams (75%) and the in-class tests (25%). A minimum score of 5 out of 10 in the Written Exams is required for this weighting to be applied. Written exams are recoverable, but in-class tests are not.
